svg.title: Cardiomyocytes in cardiac fibrosis
svg.desc: Editable 16:9 light-mode vector literature synthesis of 12 cardiomyocyte findings from 11 papers. Three panels show injury and stress programs, signals between cardiac cells, and protection and repair potential. Numbered references link to verified publication identities; hover for paper details. Human spatial and transcriptomic associations are distinguished from interventions. BMP7 cycling markers are not equated with completed adult regeneration.

Llewelyn Roderick\"\",2025,Genome Medicine,Location and aetiology are determinants of fibroplast activation and heterogeneity in the failing human heart,https://doi.org/10.1186/s13073-025-01580-z,Human Ischemic Cardiomyopathy (ICM) and Dilated Cardiomyopathy (DCM) left ventricular myocardium and infarct scar,Adult human cardiomyopathytes (paracrine signaling source in LV myocardium),\"\"How does etiology (ICM vs DCM) and spatial location dictate fibroplast subpopulations, myofibroblast differentiation, and paracrine cross-talk with cardiomyocytes under mechanical/inflammatory load?\"\",\"\"Primary research (human tissue transcriptomics, spatial profiling, cell-cell interaction modeling)\";\" Excerpts available in notebook\"\"\";;;;", "Original Paper ID": "CF001"}], "findings": [{"Finding ID": "CF066-CM-F01", "Paper ID": "CF066", "Species / System / Model / Time": "Human / hiPSC-CM (hCM), primary hCF, hEC / 2D cell culture & 3D microtissues (hMT) / 7 days", "Cardiomyocyte State & Interaction Direction": "Normoxic mature hCM -> Paracrine EV secretion -> hCF", "Signal / Intervention": "Endogenous hCM-derived extracellular vesicle (EV) miR-24-3p vs anti-miR-24-3p transfection in hCMs", "Experiment / Readout": "Real-time PCR for miRNA expression; Western blot for collagen-1 C-peptide and periostin (POSTN); Immunofluorescence for Vimentin/cTnT area ratio", "Observed Result": "hCMs expressed high baseline miR-24-3p (ranked 2nd most abundant miRNA in normal human heart). Transfection of hCMs with anti-miR-24-3p prior to 3D microtissue assembly increased TGF-beta1-induced Vimentin+/cTnT+ area ratio and conditioned media collagen-1 C-peptide level; POSTN protein level was unchanged.", "Evidence Category": "Functional perturbation", "Interpretation / Untested Link": "hCMs act as the primary cardiac reservoir of miR-24-3p, secreting EV cargo to suppress hCF activation under baseline conditions; downstream signaling in recipient hCFs involves predicted targeting of FURIN, CCND1, and SMAD4 transcripts.", "Search Tags": "miR-24-3p; extracellular vesicles; paracrine inhibition; myofibroblast conversion; collagen secretion; hiPSC-CM", "Source Citation & Figure/Panel": "CF066; Fig. 1A, 1D, 4A-E", "Review Status": "AI-extracted; awaiting source review"}, {"Finding ID": "CF066-CM-F02", "Paper ID": "CF066", "Species / System / Model / Time": "Human / 3D cardiac microtissues (hMT) and ex vivo cardiac slices (hCS) / Ischemia-simulating conditions (1% O2 hypoxia, serum starvation, 500 uM isoproterenol) / 7 days", "Cardiomyocyte State & Interaction Direction": "Ischemic/hypoxic hCM -> Paracrine EV secretion -> hCF", "Signal / Intervention": "Hypoxia/ischemia-simulating culture conditions; Berberine (BBR) pharmacological treatment", "Experiment / Readout": "Droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) for EV miR-24-3p cargo; RNAScope in situ hybridization; Immunocytochemistry for alpha-SMA and lipofuscin", "Observed Result": "Ischemia-simulating conditions decreased miR-24-3p levels in hCM-secreted EVs, hMTs, and ex vivo hCSs. EVs secreted by hypoxic hCMs failed to prevent TGF-beta1-induced hCF alpha-SMA expression. Pharmacological BBR increased miR-24-3p in hMTs and EVs, reducing interstitial Vimentin+/cTnT+ area ratio, collagen-1 C-peptide, and POSTN; anti-miR-24-3p co-treatment prevented BBR antifibrotic action. Post-mortem RNAScope showed reduced myocardial miR-24-3p in human AMI hearts vs non-MI controls.", "Evidence Category": "Functional perturbation / Observational", "Interpretation / Untested Link": "Ischemic stress downregulates CM EV miR-24-3p release, relieving baseline suppression on hCF target genes (FURIN, CCND1, SMAD4) and accelerating fibrosis.", "Search Tags": "hypoxia; ischemia; extracellular vesicles; Berberine; microtissues; human cardiac slices; AMI post-mortem", "Source Citation & Figure/Panel": "CF066; Fig. 6A-F, 7A-F, 8A-F", "Review Status": "AI-extracted; awaiting source review"}, {"Finding ID": "CF068-CM-F01", "Paper ID": "CF068", "Species / System / Model / Time": "Mouse / In vivo LAD coronary artery 30-min ischemia followed by 5 weeks reperfusion / Transgenic CM-p16 KO vs WT", "Cardiomyocyte State & Interaction Direction": "Senescent peri-infarct adult CM -> Paracrine SASP -> Interstitial fibroblasts & remodeling", "Signal / Intervention": "Cardiomyocyte-specific deletion of CDKN2A/p16 (CM-p16 KO)", "Experiment / Readout": "Cardiac MRI (EF, EDV, ESV, LV mass, scar size); Immunofluorescence (p16+ CMs, p21+ CMs, telomere-associated foci TAF); Myocardial cytokine array (IL-6, INF-gamma, G-CSF); SA-beta-gal staining", "Observed Result": "CM-p16 KO mice exhibited significantly decreased p16+ and p21+ CMs and reduced telomere-associated foci (TAF) in the peri-infarct region 5 weeks post-IR. LV ejection fraction was significantly increased, attributed to preserved LV end-systolic volume (end-diastolic volume was non-significantly different). Scar size was significantly reduced. LV indexed mass and mean CM cross-sectional area were non-significantly different between KO and WT. Myocardial IL-6 protein was significantly reduced, with trends toward decreased INF-gamma and G-CSF. Interstitial p16+ and SA-beta-gal+ non-CM cells in the peri-infarct zone were significantly reduced.", "Evidence Category": "Functional perturbation", "Interpretation / Untested Link": "Senescent CMs drive adverse post-MI remodeling and scar expansion via paracrine SASP secretion (e.g., IL-6), spreading senescence to adjacent interstitial fibroblasts; CM senescence does not directly drive physiological/pathological CM hypertrophy in this acute IR setting.", "Search Tags": "p16 (CDKN2A); senescent cardiomyocytes; ischemia-reperfusion; scar size; SASP; IL-6; ejection fraction", "Source Citation & Figure/Panel": "CF068; Fig. 1A-J, 2A-I", "Review Status": "AI-extracted; awaiting source review"}, {"Finding ID": "CF069-CM-F01", "Paper ID": "CF069", "Species / System / Model / Time": "Mouse / In vivo Isoproterenol-induced sympathetic stress (ISO, 5 mg/kg) / Days 1, 3, and 7 post-injection / Transgenic CM-specific Nox4 KO (Nox4CM-/-) vs WT; GKT137831 inhibitor", "Cardiomyocyte State & Interaction Direction": "Sympathetically stressed adult CM -> Mitochondrial ROS -> Resident macrophage activation & Fibroblast conversion", "Signal / Intervention": "Cardiomyocyte-specific genetic Nox4 deletion (Nox4CM-/-) or pharmacological NOX4 inhibition (GKT137831)", "Experiment / Readout": "Immunofluorescence co-localization (NOX4 & ATP5G); Spectral flow cytometry for macrophage subpopulations (CCR2- MHCIIhi CX3CR1hi vs CCR2- MHCIIlo CX3CR1lo); Picrosirius red collagen quantification; Echocardiography (diastolic filling pattern); Annexin V / PI flow cytometry", "Observed Result": "ISO treatment induced a 5.8-fold increase in CM NOX4 and a 9.1-fold increase in mitochondrial NOX4 co-localization in WT hearts at day 1. Targeted source checks do not constitute a systematic full-text audit.", "Senesi: CM-derived EV miR-24-3p and recipient fibroblast targets are supported by human cell and microtissue perturbations. Berberine is an experimental tissue-model intervention; patient observations do not demonstrate treatment efficacy.", "Redgrave: CM-specific p16 deletion reduced scar and senescence measures and improved systolic function after mouse I/R. Whole-heart IL6 and interstitial marker changes do not isolate direct CM-to-fibroblast IL6-mediated senescence transmission. This is not a cell-specific senolytic treatment.", "Vendrov: CM-specific Nox4 knockout supports NOX4 attribution. GKT137831 inhibits NOX1/4 and is not NOX4-selective. No increase in measured death markers is narrower than proving the absence of CM death. MHCII/CX3CR1 markers describe model-specific resident macrophage states, not universal functional lineages.", "Ko: HTRA3 is a fibroblast-derived extracellular regulator of TGF-beta; it is not a CM-intrinsic product. CM stress, DNA-damage, p53 and secretory pathways are supported by perturbations. Single-cell trajectories are not lineage fate maps.", "Da Silva: reporter activity demonstrates a CM response to RA; Aldh1a1/a2/a3 synthesis ablation increases CM apoptosis but is not proof that CMs are the source of RA. Tgm2/Ace1 are candidates, not validated causal survival effectors.", "Gladka: ischemic CM ZEB2 promotes secreted TMSB4/PTMA and endothelial activity. Conditioned-medium experiments and CM-specific gain/loss support the pro-vascular role; the factors are not drawn as direct collagen-degrading therapies.", "Wong: physical CM-macrophage contacts and focal adhesion proteins were observed; stretch-dependent macrophage TRPV4 regulates growth-factor programs. Depletion worsens genetic mouse DCM. Individual growth factors are not each assumed to explain the complete in-vivo phenotype.", "Bongiovanni: BMP7 increases cycling readouts in post-mitotic mouse settings; neonatal culture and zebrafish experiments support regenerative biology. Adult Ki67/BrdU/AuroraB alone do not establish completed adult CM cytokinesis, new muscle mass, durable functional regeneration, or clinical benefit. The figure deliberately states cycling rather than complete adult regeneration.", "Simonson: the source study includes 7 ICM and 8 non-failing hearts, with >99,000 nuclei in non-infarct LV, and integration with other cardiomyopathy data. Erroneous supplied ICM sample counts and nucleus totals are not reproduced. Ligand-receptor analysis is inferred communication, not a causal CM-sender perturbation.", "Youness: etiology- and location-dependent human fibroblast activation/spatial niches are context for CM interactions. Direct CM-specific IL1 or TGF-beta signaling into fibroblasts is not established by this spatial association.", "Arrow direction summarizes pathways within the stated experiments; the three panels are a thematic layout, not a universal temporal sequence or a combined clinical regimen."], "finding_coverage": {"injury-patterns-and-matrix": ["1-s2.0-S0098299718300670-CM-F01"], "cardiomyocyte-senescence": ["CF068-CM-F01"], "nox4-immune-fibrosis": ["CF069-CM-F01"], "vesicle-mir24-antifibrotic-brake": ["CF066-CM-F01", "CF066-CM-F02"], "zeb2-endothelial-repair": ["CF071-CM-F01"], "resident-macrophage-mechanosensing": ["1-s2.0-S1074761321002892-CM-F01"], "fibroblast-htra3-and-cm-stress": ["CF021-CM-F01"], "retinoic-acid-cardiomyocyte-survival": ["CF070-CM-F01"], "bmp7-cardiomyocyte-cycling": ["1-s2.0-S221112472400490X-CM-F01"], "human-atlas-and-spatial-context": ["CF004-CM-F01", "CF001-CM-F01"]}}
svg.text: Injury responses, intercellular signals and experimental pathways that connect muscle-cell stress to fibrosis and repair

g.title:
Review context: necrotic myocardial injury releases DAMPs and recruits immune responses leading to replacement scar, whereas chronic nonlethal CM stress promotes paracrine interstitial/perivascular matrix remodeling. ECM disruption can also threaten CM survival. Reparative scar stabilizes tissue after muscle loss.
Original extraction IDs: 1-s2.0-S0098299718300670-CM-F01. Original unreviewed extraction and interpretation notes are embedded in SVG metadata.
g.desc: Review context: necrotic myocardial injury releases DAMPs and recruits immune responses leading to replacement scar, whereas chronic nonlethal CM stress promotes paracrine interstitial/perivascular matrix remodeling. ECM disruption can also threaten CM survival. Reparative scar stabilizes tissue after muscle loss.
g.text: Two routes from CM injury to fibrosis

a.aria-label: Reference 9: Frangogiannis (2019). Cardiac fibrosis: Cell biological mechanisms, molecular pathways and therapeutic opportunities
a.title: [9] Frangogiannis (2019). Cardiac fibrosis: Cell biological mechanisms, molecular pathways and therapeutic opportunities. Molecular Aspects of Medicine. DOI: 10.1016/j.mam.2018.07.001

g.text: Scar stabilizes lost muscle; diffuse matrix increases stiffness.

g.title:
Mouse CM-specific p16 deletion after ischemia/reperfusion reduced senescence markers, scar size and interstitial senescence markers and improved ejection fraction. Whole-heart IL6 declined; direct CM-to-fibroblast IL6 causality was not isolated.
Original extraction IDs: CF068-CM-F01. Original unreviewed extraction and interpretation notes are embedded in SVG metadata.
g.desc: Mouse CM-specific p16 deletion after ischemia/reperfusion reduced senescence markers, scar size and interstitial senescence markers and improved ejection fraction. Whole-heart IL6 declined; direct CM-to-fibroblast IL6 causality was not isolated.

a.aria-label: Reference 2: Redgrave et al. (2023). Senescent cardiomyocytes contribute to cardiac dysfunction following myocardial infarction
a.title: [2] Redgrave et al. (2023). Senescent cardiomyocytes contribute to cardiac dysfunction following myocardial infarction. npj Aging. DOI: 10.1038/s41514-023-00113-5

g.text: CM-specific p16 loss in mouse I/R
Interstitial senescence markers and whole-heart IL-6 fall.
Direct CM → fibroblast IL-6 causality remains untested.

g.title:
In mouse sympathetic stress, CM mitochondrial NOX4/ROS favors resident CCR2-negative MHCII-high/CX3CR1-high macrophage states and interstitial fibrosis. CM-Nox4 knockout limits collagen deposition and preserves diastolic function. No increase was detected in the measured CM death markers. GKT137831 is a dual NOX1/4 inhibitor.
Original extraction IDs: CF069-CM-F01. Original unreviewed extraction and interpretation notes are embedded in SVG metadata.
g.desc: In mouse sympathetic stress, CM mitochondrial NOX4/ROS favors resident CCR2-negative MHCII-high/CX3CR1-high macrophage states and interstitial fibrosis. CM-Nox4 knockout limits collagen deposition and preserves diastolic function. No increase was detected in the measured CM death markers. GKT137831 is a dual NOX1/4 inhibitor.
g.text: NOX4 links stress to immune fibrosis

a.aria-label: Reference 3: Vendrov et al. (2023). Cardiomyocyte NOX4 regulates resident macrophage-mediated inflammation and diastolic dysfunction in stress cardiomyopathy
a.title: [3] Vendrov et al. (2023). Cardiomyocyte NOX4 regulates resident macrophage-mediated inflammation and diastolic dysfunction in stress cardiomyopathy. Redox Biology. DOI: 10.1016/j.redox.2023.102937

g.text: ISO stress favors MHCIIhi / CX3CR1hi macrophage states.
CM-Nox4 loss: collagen ↓; diastolic function preserved.
No increase detected in measured CM-death markers.
GKT137831 supports these effects; it inhibits NOX1/4.

g.title:
Human CM-derived extracellular vesicles carrying miR-24-3p inhibit fibroblast activation with FURIN/CCND1/SMAD4 targets. Simulated ischemia depletes EV miR-24 and weakens this inhibition. Berberine restores miR-24 and decreases fibrotic readouts in tissue models, and anti-miR blocks its effect. Patient AMI findings are observational.
Original extraction IDs: CF066-CM-F01, CF066-CM-F02. Original unreviewed extraction and interpretation notes are embedded in SVG metadata.
g.desc: Human CM-derived extracellular vesicles carrying miR-24-3p inhibit fibroblast activation with FURIN/CCND1/SMAD4 targets. Simulated ischemia depletes EV miR-24 and weakens this inhibition. Berberine restores miR-24 and decreases fibrotic readouts in tissue models, and anti-miR blocks its effect. Patient AMI findings are observational.

a.aria-label: Reference 1: Senesi et al. (2025). miR-24-3p secreted as extracellular vesicle cargo by cardiomyocytes inhibits fibrosis in human cardiac microtissues
a.title: [1] Senesi et al. (2025). miR-24-3p secreted as extracellular vesicle cargo by cardiomyocytes inhibits fibrosis in human cardiac microtissues. Cardiovascular Research. DOI: 10.1093/cvr/cvae243

g.text: Ischemia lowers EV miR-24-3p; the antifibrotic brake weakens.
Berberine restores EV miR-24 and lowers fibrosis readouts.
Anti-miR-24 blocks this effect in human microtissues.
Human cells, microtissues and slices; AMI observations.

g.title:
Ischemic CM ZEB2 induces TMSB4 and PTMA secretion and stimulates endothelial activity. CM-specific gain/loss and conditioned-medium or knockdown experiments support a pro-vascular role after mouse ischemic injury.
Original extraction IDs: CF071-CM-F01. Original unreviewed extraction and interpretation notes are embedded in SVG metadata.
g.desc: Ischemic CM ZEB2 induces TMSB4 and PTMA secretion and stimulates endothelial activity. CM-specific gain/loss and conditioned-medium or knockdown experiments support a pro-vascular role after mouse ischemic injury.
g.text: ZEB2 couples injured CMs to angiogenesis

a.aria-label: Reference 5: Gladka et al. (2021). Cardiomyocytes stimulate angiogenesis after ischemic injury in a ZEB2-dependent manner
a.title: [5] Gladka et al. (2021). Cardiomyocytes stimulate angiogenesis after ischemic injury in a ZEB2-dependent manner. Nature Communications. DOI: 10.1038/s41467-020-20361-3

g.text: CM-specific ZEB2 gain / loss supports a pro-vascular role.

g.title:
Resident CCR2-negative macrophages physically contact CMs via focal-adhesion-associated structures. Mechanical stretch activates macrophage TRPV4-dependent IGF1/PDGFC/HBEGF programs. Depleting resident macrophages in genetic mouse DCM decreases coronary vascularity, increases fibrosis and worsens function and survival.
Original extraction IDs: 1-s2.0-S1074761321002892-CM-F01. Original unreviewed extraction and interpretation notes are embedded in SVG metadata.
g.desc: Resident CCR2-negative macrophages physically contact CMs via focal-adhesion-associated structures. Mechanical stretch activates macrophage TRPV4-dependent IGF1/PDGFC/HBEGF programs. Depleting resident macrophages in genetic mouse DCM decreases coronary vascularity, increases fibrosis and worsens function and survival.

a.aria-label: Reference 7: Wong et al. (2021). Resident cardiac macrophages mediate adaptive myocardial remodeling
a.title: [7] Wong et al. (2021). Resident cardiac macrophages mediate adaptive myocardial remodeling. Immunity. DOI: 10.1016/j.immuni.2021.07.003

g.text: IGF1 / PDGFC / HBEGF programs support adaptive remodeling.
Resident-cell depletion in genetic mouse DCM:
Vessels ↓ • fibrosis ↑ • function and survival worsen

g.title:
Fibroblast-derived HTRA3 restrains extracellular TGF-beta. Pressure overload or Htra3 loss activates CM NOX4/ROS, DNA damage and p53-linked failing/secretory programs. AAV-Htra3 or Nox4 knockdown improves mouse cardiac function; Htra3 delivery also reduces fibrosis. CM p53 loss suppresses secretory-pathway genes.
Original extraction IDs: CF021-CM-F01. Original unreviewed extraction and interpretation notes are embedded in SVG metadata.
g.desc: Fibroblast-derived HTRA3 restrains extracellular TGF-beta. Pressure overload or Htra3 loss activates CM NOX4/ROS, DNA damage and p53-linked failing/secretory programs. AAV-Htra3 or Nox4 knockdown improves mouse cardiac function; Htra3 delivery also reduces fibrosis. CM p53 loss suppresses secretory-pathway genes.

a.aria-label: Reference 6: Ko et al. (2022). Cardiac fibroblasts regulate the development of heart failure via Htra3-TGF-β-IGFBP7 axis
a.title: [6] Ko et al. (2022). Cardiac fibroblasts regulate the development of heart failure via Htra3-TGF-β-IGFBP7 axis. Nature Communications. DOI: 10.1038/s41467-022-30630-y

g.text: Pressure overload weakens this extracellular brake.
AAV-Htra3 or Nox4 knockdown improves mouse function.
Htra3 delivery also reduces pressure-overload fibrosis.
Mouse perturbations; HTRA3 originates in fibroblasts.

g.title:
Retinoic acid reporter activity is directly observed in adult mouse CMs after MI. Aldh1a1/a2/a3 synthesis loss increases CM apoptosis. This does not identify CMs as the RA source. Tgm2/Ace1 remain candidate downstream targets, not proven survival effectors.
Original extraction IDs: CF070-CM-F01. Original unreviewed extraction and interpretation notes are embedded in SVG metadata.
g.desc: Retinoic acid reporter activity is directly observed in adult mouse CMs after MI. Aldh1a1/a2/a3 synthesis loss increases CM apoptosis. This does not identify CMs as the RA source. Tgm2/Ace1 remain candidate downstream targets, not proven survival effectors.

a.title: [4] Da Silva et al. (2021). Retinoic acid signaling is directly activated in cardiomyocytes and protects mouse hearts from apoptosis after myocardial infarction. eLife. DOI: 10.7554/eLife.68280

g.text: RA reporter activity rises in adult CMs after MI.
Tgm2 / Ace1: candidate targets; survival mechanism unresolved.

g.title:
BMP7 activates SMAD5, ERK and AKT and increases CM cycling readouts in mouse cultures and after adult mouse MI; zebrafish loss/gain experiments support post-injury cycling. Adult cell-cycle markers alone do not establish completed adult CM division or full functional regeneration.
Original extraction IDs: 1-s2.0-S221112472400490X-CM-F01. Original unreviewed extraction and interpretation notes are embedded in SVG metadata.
g.desc: BMP7 activates SMAD5, ERK and AKT and increases CM cycling readouts in mouse cultures and after adult mouse MI; zebrafish loss/gain experiments support post-injury cycling. Adult cell-cycle markers alone do not establish completed adult CM division or full functional regeneration.

g.title:
Human single-nucleus profiles show shared failing-CM transcriptional states across cardiomyopathies. Human fibroblast spatial activation depends on etiology and scar versus remote location. Ligand-receptor and neighborhood associations contextualize interactions without demonstrating a CM-specific causal mechanism.
Original extraction IDs: CF004-CM-F01, CF001-CM-F01. Original unreviewed extraction and interpretation notes are embedded in SVG metadata.
g.desc: Human single-nucleus profiles show shared failing-CM transcriptional states across cardiomyopathies. Human fibroblast spatial activation depends on etiology and scar versus remote location. Ligand-receptor and neighborhood associations contextualize interactions without demonstrating a CM-specific causal mechanism.
g.text: Shared failing-CM states and scar / remote niches.
Human profiles; CM-specific causality remains untested.

svg.text: Cardiomyocytes shape fibrosis through stress, vesicle cargo, vascular signals and reciprocal cellular feedback.
Sources: both supplied CSVs • 12 findings / 11 papers • publication identities checked; extraction IDs and interpretation notes embedded.
Evidence distinguishes human observations from model interventions. Cell cycling alone does not establish completed adult regeneration.
CM: cardiomyocyte; EV: extracellular vesicle; ECM: extracellular matrix; MI: infarction; I/R: ischemia/reperfusion; ISO: isoproterenol; DCM: dilated cardiomyopathy.
